mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in declining rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0%, it indicates a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE exceeds 7.0%, the S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS rise, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by strong GDP growth and low unemployment, the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns as investors anticipate continued corporate earnings momentum and avoid premature risk-off behavior.
failure_condition: In periods meeting the trigger condition (GDPC1>2.0 and UNRATE<6.0), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, correlating with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO's 5-day forward return signal remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or INDPRO's direction is not predictive of SPX returns in more than 60% of observations.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals heightened inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 achieves positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy coupled with a strengthening labor market, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through improved economic growth expectations and lower risk premiums.
regime_hint: monetary easing with labor market strength
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines and UNRATE falls simultaneously, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime marked by declining industrial production and rising inflation, the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as cost-push inflation erodes corporate margins and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: In periods meeting the trigger condition (INDPRO<99.0 and CPIAUCSL>2.5), the S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC for the regime condition falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
